mainRule: The agent should only have one feature in in_progress at any time

status_legend.in_progress: The feature is the current active task.
status_legend.blocked: Work cannot continue until a documented blocker is resolved.
status_legend.passing: Required verification has passed and evidence is recorded.

features.title: Add --severity CRITICAL to trivy fs alongside the existing stream filter
features.user_visible_behavior: Trivy pre-filters to CRITICAL before the report ever reaches the app, so the report written to disk is smaller and cheaper to stream-parse. The stream parser still filters, counts and caps independently, so neither layer is a single point of trust for what reaches Redis.
evidence: npm run test -> 12 suites / 127 tests passed, 2026-08-31
npx eslint on both changed files -> No issues found (exit 0), 2026-08-31

End-to-end via `docker compose up --build`: scan reached FINISHED and reported a non-zero CRITICAL count, confirming the pinned TRIVY_VERSION v0.74.0 accepts --severity CRITICAL and does not over-filter. Run manually by the user, not by an automated test.
features.notes: Implements the third trade-off documented in README 'Trade-offs and design notes'. The Severity !== 'CRITICAL' check in trivy-stream-parser.service.ts is deliberately retained: it is boundary validation against an external process, not a redundant internal invariant.

features.title: Store every CRITICAL finding in Redis and serve it via offset/limit pagination
features.user_visible_behavior: The full vulnerability list can be browsed page by page instead of being capped at the first 2000 findings. `criticalVulnerabilities(offset, limit)` returns a slice, `criticalVulnerabilityCount` is the true total, and the web UI pages through it with Prev/Next.
evidence: npm run test -> 13 suites / 149 tests passed, 2026-08-31
npx tsc --noEmit -> No errors found (exit 0); npx eslint on src/ and test/ -> exit 0

OOM self-test on a 539MB / 112,500-CRITICAL fixture: all 112,500 findings streamed to the sink in 215 batches, largest batch 525. Parses successfully down to --max-old-space-size=25, which retaining the findings could not do - direct evidence the buffer stays bounded.

Memory delta measured against the previous truncating parser on the same machine and fixture: ~203MB RSS before, ~214MB after (~5%). The ~124MB figure previously recorded in README does not reproduce on this machine even with the old code.
features.notes: Findings move out of the scan:<id> JSON record into a scan:<id>:vulns Redis list, written in batches during the stream parse so nothing accumulates in JS memory. Removes MAX_RETAINED_VULNERABILITIES and the criticalVulnerabilitiesTruncated flag. Not verified by automated tests: the LRANGE/RPUSH path against a live Redis (the ioredis client is mocked throughout) and the browser behaviour of the Prev/Next controls.
